'''Miyake Shrine''' (みやけじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Miyake-chō, {{ill|Kameoka, Kyoto|Q633996|qid=Q633996}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|Q120730|qid=Q120730}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}. Its former rank under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=old shrine ranking}} was {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

It is also called "Miyake Inari," and was formerly called "Mure Inari" and "Kusawake Inari."

=== Enshrined deities ===
* '''{{ill|Ukanomitama|de|Ukanomitama|eo|Ukanomitama|fr|Uka-no-Mitama|ja|ウカノミタマ|mni|ꯎꯀꯅꯣꯃꯤꯇꯃ|ru|Ука-но митама|simple|Ukanomitama|sv|Ukanomitama|th|อูกาโนมิตามะ|zh|宇迦之御魂神|qid=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto}}''' (うかのみたまのみこと)<ref>Deities from precinct information board.</ref>
* '''{{ill|Wakumusubi|lt=Wakumusubi|UNKNOWN|qid=Q10921330|lt=Wakumusubi-no-Mikoto}}''' (わくむすびのみこと)
* '''{{ill|Ukemochi|Q2280323|qid=Q2280323|lt=Toyoukemochi-no-Mikoto}}''' (とようけもちのみこと)
All three are deities related to grain.

=== History ===
[[File:Miyake-jinja (Kameoka) keidai.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Precinct<br />Honden in center, maiden on left, Toyouke Ōkami on right.]]
Founding is unknown. It is said to derive from establishment of a {{ill|Miyake|Q11465761|qid=Q11465761}} (imperial direct estate) in this area. Though local relation is unclear, the '{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}' records that in {{ill|Emperor Ankan|Q241765|qid=Q241765}} 2 ({{ill|535|Q31019|qid=Q31019}}?) a miyake called "Soshiki" was established in Tanba<ref>'Nihon Shoki,' Emperor Ankan year 2, fifth month entry: "... established Soshiki miyake in Tanba Province." ([https://www.seisaku.bz/nihonshoki/shoki_18.html Nihon Shoki Vol.18 Emperor Ankan Chronicle] via full-text search).</ref>. It is also argued that this area was the center where the Kuwata district office stood, based on old reading of district office ({{ill|Gunga (Japan)|Q11643230|qid=Q11643230}}) as "kōri no miyake," the broad flat terrain, and presence of this shrine suggesting miyake existence<ref>From precinct information board.</ref><ref>'Place Names of Kyoto Prefecture,' entries for Miyake village and Miyake Shrine.</ref>. Many kiln remains, thought to have produced pottery for rituals, have been found nearby<ref>[https://tanbarakuichi.sakura.ne.jp/shrine/kameoka/06.html#k059 Miyake Shrine] (Tanba shrines, personal site).</ref>.

In the mid-Heian '{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}' {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Jinmyōchō}}, it is listed as "Miyake Shrine" in {{ill|Kuwada district|Q11537600|qid=Q11537600}}, {{ill|Tanba Province|Q954511|qid=Q954511}}, and ranked as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}.

It is said to have once held a vast shrine precinct of one chō square, but shrank due to war fires in the Tenshō era and other fires including {{ill|Kanbun (era)|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228}} 3 ({{ill|1663|Q7577|qid=Q7577}}). The current shrine was rebuilt in {{ill|Enpō|Q1145735|qid=Q1145735}} 1 ({{ill|1673|Q7617|qid=Q7617}}), and an outer covering structure was added in {{ill|Genroku|ar|فترة غنروكو|cs|Genroku|de|Genroku|es|Genroku|fa|گنروکو|fr|Ère Genroku|id|Genroku|it|Genroku|ja|元禄|ko|겐로쿠|pt|Genroku|ru|Гэнроку|simple|Genroku|sk|Genroku|sr|Генроку|sv|Genroku|tr|Genroku|zh|元祿|qid=Q1325001}} 11 ({{ill|1698|Q7706|qid=Q7706}}).

In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 6 it was ranked {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}} under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine ranking system}}, and in Meiji 40 became a designated village shrine<ref name=chosa/>.
